title: The Sham of Hustle Culture.
summary: Newsletter arguing gurus market to desire and fear, profit only from course sales, offer advice too generic to work, and that lifestyle ads are not credible.

assertions.quote: they are more importantly marketing to fear; The fear of not being successful, which is often a more powerful driving force.

verdicts.note: Consistent with consumer-protection research on business-opportunity fraud and loss-aversion marketing.

assertions.quote: the only money they are actually making comes from the courses they sell.
99% of videos you see advertising the lifestyle of private jets and tons of money are not credible
The reason their advice and schemes (almost) never work is that it is too general.
If you put in enough hours into something you are passionate about, success and money will follow.

verdicts.note: Motivational framing; passion is neither necessary nor sufficient for income.

assertions.quote: The Fake Gurus would never make any money if their clients actually got rich and successful.

verdicts.note: Upsell funnels are documented, but customers who succeed become testimonials, so the incentive is mixed.

The FTC alleges Nudge's seminars were mostly designed to sell additional training rather than help consumers make money, with an escalating ladder to $40,000 packages; shows the upsell dependence, not that failure itself is required.
